summary: Inclusive pricing thresholds became exclusive when the tier lookup was made table-driven
engine: claude-opus-5 (local dry run — no Copilot seat in this environment)
rootCauseHypothesis: ff4ddce "refactor(pricing): table-driven tier lookup" replaced the if-chain in tierRateFor with a loop over TIERS and changed the comparison from >= to >. The spec in docs/pricing-rules.md defines the 100 and 500 thresholds as inclusive, so a subtotal of exactly 100 now falls through to 0% and exactly 500 falls through to the 10% tier. The same commit changed isCouponValid from <= to <, which is the reported coupon-rejected-on-expiry-date behaviour. The commit message claims behaviour is unchanged; the existing tests only cover 99, 250 and 900, so no boundary is exercised and the regression shipped green.

suspectFiles.reason: tierRateFor uses `subtotal > tier.threshold` at line 18 and isCouponValid uses `<` at line 28; both should be inclusive per the spec
authoritative spec — states thresholds are inclusive and coupons valid up to and including expiresAt
covers 99 / 250 / 900 only; no case at a threshold, which is why the regression passed CI

relatedCommits.subject: refactor(pricing): table-driven tier lookup — introduced the regression
feat(pricing): tier discounts and loyalty coupons — the correct >= / <= original

steps.title: Confirm the regression with a failing test before touching the code
steps.detail: Add boundary assertions to sample-app/test/pricing.test.js: tierRateFor(100) === 0.1, tierRateFor(500) === 0.2, and isCouponValid({ expiresAt: T }, T) === true. Run them against the current code and watch all three fail — this pins the defect and stops it returning.
steps.validation: `cd sample-app && node --test` reports 3 failures naming the boundary cases

steps.title: Restore the inclusive tier comparison
steps.detail: In tierRateFor, change `if (subtotal > tier.threshold)` to `if (subtotal >= tier.threshold)`. Keep the TIERS table and the descending order — the table refactor itself was fine, only the operator regressed.

steps.title: Restore the inclusive coupon expiry check
steps.detail: In isCouponValid, change `now.getTime() < new Date(coupon.expiresAt).getTime()` to `<=`, matching "valid up to and including" in docs/pricing-rules.md. This is the customer-reported half of the ticket and is a separate line from step 2 — do not stop after fixing the tiers.
steps.validation: isCouponValid({ expiresAt: T }, T) === true and isCouponValid({ expiresAt: T }, T + 1ms) === false

steps.title: Add a guard so the TIERS table cannot silently reorder
steps.detail: tierRateFor returns the first matching tier, so it depends on TIERS being sorted by descending threshold — an implicit invariant that the table refactor introduced and nothing enforces. Either sort defensively inside the function or assert the ordering in a test.
steps.validation: a test that reverses TIERS still yields 0.2 for a 900 subtotal

steps.title: Check for other callers relying on the exclusive behaviour
steps.detail: grep for tierRateFor, isCouponValid and priceOrder across the repo before shipping. If any caller compensated for the off-by-one (for example passing subtotal + 0.01), that workaround now double-counts and must be removed in the same change.
steps.validation: no remaining caller adjusts the subtotal or expiry before calling in

tests: tierRateFor at exactly 100 and exactly 500 (the two thresholds from the spec)
tierRateFor just below each threshold — 99.99 and 499.99 — to prove the fix does not over-discount
isCouponValid at exactly expiresAt, and one millisecond after
priceOrder({ subtotal: 100 }) totals 90.00 end to end
priceOrder with a tier discount plus a coupon that would exceed 50% stays capped at 50%
rollback: The change is two comparison operators plus tests, confined to sample-app/src/pricing.js. Revert the fix commit to return to current behaviour; no data migration, no config, no persisted state is involved.
